items.title: Bob Wilber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998
items.q: I was asked by George Wein to play a concert at Carnegie Hall in a tribute to Bechet with Jon Faddis and the Carnegie Hall Big Band.

ctx.x: Yeah, it was. But you know what some of the jazz critics said? They said, “You’re tampering with a great record, you have no right to do that. I mean the second one of course was a Bechet masterpiece from 1944, four minutes of totally improvised blues, in which he tells his story, as he used to say when he was teaching me. He starts out with a very simple blues in the low register. Each chorus he builds, he goes up, he goes up and up and up. He finally reaches one of the highest notes on the clarinet, high E…
